column1: # Each of raylib's examples not written here, and a written one that differs, read by
# build/examples-table.py. A line is a name, a state and a note, apart by tabs. The state is can
# (everything it calls the flat API carries, and nobody has written it yet), part (written, leaving
# out what the note names), missing (the note names what the flat API lacks) or n/a (the note says
# why it is not a thing a program here does), and a written one may be marked moves (the note says
# why its picture moves by the clock or the device from run to run, and the build workflow's
# measure against raylib leaves it out). C#'s own strings, files and memory stand in for
# raylib's TextFormat, its file functions and MemAlloc, which count as carried. build/examples-table.py
# --triage prints a first line for an example that has none.
